text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Police will launch a 17-day operation to avoid a repeat of last year's high death toll in road accidents during the twin festivities of Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr.
-- A former schoolbus driver begins serving his nine-month jail sentence nearly 13 years after being convicted of dangerous driving in an accident that killed 19 of his passengers.
-- Buses in Kuala Lumpur will have to keep to a special lane along certain roads at all times from February 15, in a move designed to ease the city's traffic congestion.
-- The Education Ministry has proposed a new certificate to prepare weak secondary students for work as soon as they leave school.

-- The seven million ringgit log smuggling case in eastern Sabah state has taken a new twist when Deputy Chief Minister Abdul Ghapur Salleh accused Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik of attempting to cover the mistakes of his ministry.
-- Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik wants Penang Port and Port Klang to speed up their clearing of bulk cargo, which now takes more than two days.
